title: Weather Alert: Typhoon Champi Moves Away, but Heavy Rain Continues in the North
summaryZh: ⚠️ 颱風羌彼遠離，陸警預計週六晚解除；北部山區仍有豪雨。
summaryHi: ⚠️ तूफ़ान चाम्पी दूर जा रहा है, पर उत्तरी पहाड़ों में भारी बारिश जारी रहेगी।
summaryEs: ⚠️ El tifón Champi se aleja, pero sigue la lluvia intensa en las montañas del norte.

summaryEn: ⚠️ Typhoon Champi is leaving Taiwan, but heavy rain will continue in northern mountains until early Sunday.
paragraphs: Typhoon Champi was pulling away from Taiwan on Saturday, but the Central Weather Administration (CWA) warned that the north would face strong winds and heavy rain for several more hours.

As of 10 a.m., the storm's centre was about 170 kilometres east-northeast of Yilan County, heading north at 21 km/h, with maximum sustained winds of 126 km/h and gusts of up to 162 km/h. Forecasters expected it to weaken into a tropical storm by the afternoon. The land warning is likely to be lifted on Saturday evening, followed by the sea warning later that night.

Rainfall is gradually easing and should taper off from Saturday night into early Sunday. However, extremely heavy rain advisories remain in force for mountainous parts of Taipei, New Taipei, Taoyuan, Hsinchu and Miaoli, where the risk of landslides is high. Waves above six metres were reported off the north and east coasts.

Thirteen cities and counties, including Taipei, New Taipei, Keelung, Taoyuan, Hsinchu, Taichung, Yilan and Miaoli, declared a second straight typhoon day off on Saturday. Many international flights were cancelled or postponed, while domestic flights and ferry services were suspended.

The storm has left one person dead and 527 injured, mostly from fallen trees, power cables and billboards. Residents are urged to stay away from coasts, rivers and slopes, and travellers should confirm their plans with airlines before leaving home.
Typhoon Champi is now moving away from Taiwan. But it is still windy, and it is still raining a lot in the north.

On Saturday morning, the storm was about 170 kilometres from Yilan. It was moving north. The weather office says the land warning will end on Saturday evening. The sea warning will end on Saturday night.
On Saturday, schools and offices were closed in 13 cities and counties, like Taipei, New Taipei and Taichung. Many flights and boats were stopped.

Rain will stop slowly by Sunday morning. But the mountains near Taipei, Taoyuan, Hsinchu and Miaoli may still get very heavy rain. One person died and more than 500 people were hurt. Please stay away from beaches, rivers and mountains, and look out for fallen trees.
Typhoon Champi is moving away from Taiwan, but strong winds and heavy rain are still affecting the north, the Central Weather Administration (CWA) said on Saturday.

At 10 a.m., the storm was about 170 kilometres east-northeast of Yilan and moving north at 21 kilometres per hour. It was expected to become a weaker tropical storm in the afternoon. The CWA said the land warning should end on Saturday evening and the sea warning on Saturday night.

Rain is slowly getting lighter and should stop in most places by early Sunday. However, the mountains of Taipei, New Taipei, Taoyuan, Hsinchu and Miaoli are still under extremely heavy rain advisories, so landslides are possible.

Schools and offices were closed again on Saturday in 13 cities and counties, including Taipei, New Taipei, Keelung, Taoyuan and Taichung. Many flights to and from Taiwan were cancelled or delayed, and domestic flights and ferries were suspended. Travellers should check with their airline.
So far, one person has died and 527 have been injured, mostly by falling trees, cables and signs. Officials ask people to avoid beaches, rivers and mountain roads until the warnings end.
Typhoon Champi was pulling away from Taiwan on Saturday, but the Central Weather Administration (CWA) warned that the north would face strong winds and heavy rain for several more hours.

As of 10 a.m., the storm's centre was about 170 kilometres east-northeast of Yilan County, heading north at 21 km/h, with maximum sustained winds of 126 km/h and gusts of up to 162 km/h. Forecasters expected it to weaken into a tropical storm by the afternoon. The land warning is likely to be lifted on Saturday evening, followed by the sea warning later that night.

Rainfall is gradually easing and should taper off from Saturday night into early Sunday. However, extremely heavy rain advisories remain in force for mountainous parts of Taipei, New Taipei, Taoyuan, Hsinchu and Miaoli, where the risk of landslides is high. Waves above six metres were reported off the north and east coasts.

Thirteen cities and counties, including Taipei, New Taipei, Keelung, Taoyuan, Hsinchu, Taichung, Yilan and Miaoli, declared a second straight typhoon day off on Saturday. Many international flights were cancelled or postponed, while domestic flights and ferry services were suspended.

The storm has left one person dead and 527 injured, mostly from fallen trees, power cables and billboards. Residents are urged to stay away from coasts, rivers and slopes, and travellers should confirm their plans with airlines before leaving home.

Typhoon Champi was finally edging away from Taiwan on Saturday, though the Central Weather Administration (CWA) cautioned that its outer bands would continue to batter the north with gales and torrential downpours for some hours yet.

At 10 a.m., the storm lay roughly 170 kilometres east-northeast of Yilan County, tracking north at 21 km/h with sustained winds of 126 km/h and gusts reaching 162 km/h, after a gust exceeding 221 km/h was recorded at Sandiao Cape late on Friday. It was forecast to weaken to tropical-storm strength by the afternoon, allowing the land warning to be lifted in the evening and the sea warning overnight.

Rain should taper off from Saturday night into early Sunday, but extremely heavy rain advisories still cover mountainous areas of Taipei, New Taipei, Taoyuan, Hsinchu and Miaoli, where saturated slopes heighten the danger of landslides.

Thirteen local governments, among them Taipei, New Taipei, Keelung, Taoyuan, Taichung and Yilan, called a second consecutive typhoon day, closing schools and offices. Numerous international flights were cancelled or rescheduled, and domestic air and ferry links remained suspended.

The toll so far stands at one death and 527 injuries, largely caused by toppled trees, falling cables and dislodged billboards. Authorities advise residents to keep clear of coastlines, riverbanks and hillsides, and travellers to verify their bookings before setting out.

Typhoon Champi was gradually retreating from Taiwan on Saturday; however, the Central Weather Administration (CWA) emphasised that northern regions would remain exposed to powerful winds and intense rainfall for several more hours.

At 10 a.m., the storm was positioned approximately 170 kilometres east-northeast of Yilan County, moving northwards at 21 km/h, with maximum sustained winds of 126 km/h. It was projected to downgrade to a tropical storm by the afternoon, whereupon the land warning would be lifted in the evening and the sea warning subsequently overnight.

Precipitation is expected to diminish progressively from Saturday night into early Sunday. Nevertheless, extremely heavy rain advisories persist for mountainous districts of Taipei, New Taipei, Taoyuan, Hsinchu and Miaoli, where waterlogged terrain substantially increases the likelihood of landslides.

Thirteen cities and counties, including Taipei, New Taipei, Keelung, Taoyuan, Taichung and Yilan, declared a second consecutive typhoon day, suspending classes and office work. Numerous international flights were cancelled or postponed, and domestic flights and ferry services were halted.

The storm has so far resulted in one fatality and 527 injuries, predominantly attributable to uprooted trees, collapsing cables and detached billboards. The authorities recommend that residents avoid coastal areas, riverbanks and slopes, and that travellers confirm arrangements with their carriers prior to departure.
